annotations.title: Pick between two or three products

description: For two or three products, which one the written buy-or-wait rules put ahead, or that neither is ahead, optionally for a shopper who owns a device or uses iPhone or Android, with a budget. Each product comes with its verdict (buy_now, wait, skip, check_fit or not_enough_data), its fit with the phone given, today's retailer price and the reasons, each with its source and how sure iDevice is. A product that does not work with the phone given goes last; then the verdict decides, then the fit answer. Price alone does not put one ahead. When the rules leave two products level, review_tiebreak says whether outlets' published review scores separate them (at least two independent outlets that reviewed each, all one way, a clear margin) and lists the themes reviewers agree on, each with the outlets that reported it. purchase_today and product_for_you split the answer in two: the better purchase today on the rules, and the better product, named only on the phone or fit answer or on outlets' review scores, else No clear winner; where the companies' own figures lean one way, product_for_you says which product leads on which criteria, conditionally, and names no winner (lead null). A lead on the verdict alone (lead_basis timing) is about when to buy, not which product is better; a product that only reads BUY NOW or FINE TO BUY against NO RUSH is not a lead, and a product whose answer is not_enough_data (NEWER MODEL OUT, NOT ENOUGH DATA) is not out-bought unless the other product is its own newer model already out. The same comparison as the decision card on idevice.com. No model is involved. A line slug (for example 'samsung-galaxy-ring') names the line's newest model; when that model is not on sale the answer is for the newest model of the line that is, and resolved_to says which and why.

budget_usd.description: A price ceiling in US dollars

owned_device_slug.description: A product_slug of a device the shopper already owns, e.g. 'iphone-17'

owned_platform.description: The phone platform the shopper uses
